name: User-Agent Parser
description: Break a User-Agent string down into browser, operating system, device type and rendering engine.

examples.label: Chrome desktop
examples.value: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

examples.label: iOS Safari
examples.value: Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 18_1 like Mac OS X) AppleWebKit/605.1.15 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/18.1 Mobile/15E148 Safari/604.1

hints.output: The result distinguishes desktop, mobile, tablet and bot, and reports the rendering engine; recognition relies on built-in keyword matching, not an online database.

faq.q: Can the result be used as a device fingerprint?
faq.a: No. It only performs structural recognition; it neither fingerprints nor decides whether a User-Agent was spoofed.

faq.q: Is the UA data kept up to date?
faq.a: Not automatically. The recognition rules are a built-in snapshot updated with tool releases.

faq.q: Why is no browser detected for some User-Agents?
faq.a: Recognition relies on keyword and prefix matching. Unusual or deliberately spoofed User-Agents only yield unknown.
